title: LFU Cache
statement: Simulate an LFU cache of the given capacity. `operations` are get and put. get(key) returns the value or -1 and counts as a use. put(key, value) inserts or updates. When the cache is full, evict the least frequently used key, breaking ties by least recently used. put returns null. A capacity of 0 rejects every put.
hints: A map from key to (value, frequency) answers get in constant time.
A second map from frequency to an ordered dictionary of keys keeps each frequency bucket in LRU order.
Remember the current minimum frequency. Eviction pops the oldest key in that bucket, and a use moves a key into the next bucket.

approaches.name: Scan for the eviction victim
approaches.explanation: Track frequency and a timestamp, then scan.

approaches.name: Frequency buckets
approaches.explanation: Ordered dictionaries give LRU order inside a frequency.

editorial: get on a missing key returns -1. get on a present key increments its frequency and moves it to the most-recent end of the new bucket. If its old bucket becomes empty and it was the minimum frequency, the minimum rises by one. put of a new key evicts first when at capacity, then inserts the key at frequency 1, which becomes the new minimum.

examples.explanation: Frequency, then recency, decides the eviction.
